  "rationale": "The book's core—that works are simply deeds (not a synonym for obedience), becoming obedience only when they execute God's command (or disobedience under another lawgiver)—best unifies the printed texts without forcing them into a single soteriological slot. These texts are explained more tightly by the book's distinction than by the common reading that immediately folds every occurrence into 'fruit/evidence of the heart' or 'basis of final judgment.' The common view correctly notes the evidential function in many passages but does not account for the wage-versus-duty contrast or the neutral status of the deed prior to the governing lawgiver; the book's core does so with fewer unsupported steps. Secondary claims (e.g., that works are always 'commandment-shaped') are elaborations that may be disputed without overturning the core referent.",
